To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) there was an increase in the number of people using health websites; 2) the most popular websites were those with the most information; 3) the websites with the most information also had the most complex navigation; 4) people who were less satisfied with their health were more likely to be satisfied with their use of the health websites; and 5) people with lower levels of education and those with lower levels of computer experience had more problems with using the websites.

(i) the health internet websites are not only an information source, but also an important source for health care, and (ii) the users of these websites have a strong desire for a better control of their health care.

(a) the majority of the participants were satisfied with the information they found on the internet, (b) the participants were satisfied in general with the quality of information found on the internet and (c) participants were satisfied with their ability to evaluate information found on the web.

how consumers are using the internet for health information, and what this means for health professionals, health care organisations and the health system as a whole.
